name: Kate Headley Kirby
bio: John Fothergill's second wife, married about 1920, and by his own published account the making of him. Under the two of them the Spread Eagle at Thame became a destination restaurant; An Innkeeper's Diary (1931) credits her by name, down to the trifle. Sox's verdict is that Fothergill married her having 'apparently resolved previous emotional ambivalences', and that 'In many respects, Kate was his salvation'.
bio_note: The marriage year is ARITHMETIC, not testimony: Sox says the innkeeping life began when Fothergill was 46 - 1922, he having been born 27 February 1876 - and 'two years after' the marriage, which gives c. 1920. Sox states no wedding date and neither does Wikipedia.
